- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.4) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% to match mean reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and price is falling, model underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer to forecast to account for sentiment-driven volatility.
- Model consistently underestimates short-term mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if 30d forecast is below 70% of 18d avg, increase by 2–5% to align with historical mean reversion pattern.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.2–0.6), model often overfits recent volatility; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values to reduce noise.
- If sentiment is trending upward (e.g., 3+ consecutive >0.6), model tends to overestimate future prices; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent 18d high to avoid overbought bias.
